steelman: A company rebrand can involve more than cosmetic changes: cloud account reorganizations, billing account migrations, org hierarchy restructuring, or resource retagging sometimes accompany major brand launches and could inadvertently reset storage quota tiers or alter per-account rate limits. Additionally, if the CI pipeline resolves the storage endpoint via a custom domain updated during the rebrand, the upload target could have shifted to a storage backend with stricter per-client limits. A senior SRE investigating the temporal coincidence would reasonably ask whether any cloud account, billing, or DNS configuration changes were made as part of the rebrand launch.
mechanism_if_any: Cloud account/billing reorganization during rebrand could reset quota tiers; DNS/CDN reconfiguration during rebrand could redirect uploads to a backend with different rate limits.
notes: The xbase explicitly states 'bucket name and IAM credentials are unchanged,' which closes both steelman pathways: unchanged credentials foreclose any account-tier or quota-context change from billing/org restructuring, and an unchanged bucket name forecloses any DNS/CDN redirect to a different storage backend. The closure is thorough. No repair needed — seed passes this lens cleanly.
